final_answer:
the sky appears blue during the day due to rayleigh scattering, which is the elastic scattering of light by particles much smaller than the wavelength of the light. sunlight is composed of many wavelengths, with shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scattering more intensely than longer wavelengths (red/orange). since blue light is scattered in all directions more efficiently, it dominates the sky’s color when the sun is high, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet.  

during sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, increasing the path length. this causes more scattering of the shorter blue/violet wavelengths, leaving the longer red/orange wavelengths to reach the observer. the scattered blue is now mostly out of our line of sight, while the red/orange light becomes more prominent, creating the reddish hue of sunsets.
